content.title: About
content.content: Rice pudding is a classic dessert made from cooked rice, milk, sugar, and flavorings such as vanilla, cinnamon, or raisins. It has a smooth, creamy texture and a mildly sweet taste.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Rice pudding is known worldwide: in Italy as riso al latte, in Japan as rice porridge desserts, and in Russia as a sweet rice kissel.
Traditionally it was prepared for holidays and fasting days, often using plant‑based milks as a substitute.
Vegan versions replace dairy with coconut, almond, or oat milk, keeping the dish dairy‑free.
Some regional recipes add nuts, dried fruits, or caramelized sugar for extra flavor.
Rice pudding can be served chilled or warm, straight from the pot.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Rice provides slow‑releasing energy, helping maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains thiamine, niacin, and vitamin B6, which support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains magnesium
items.content: Magnesium aids muscle and nerve function and participates in protein synthesis.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with many desserts, rice pudding typically contains little saturated fat.

items.title: Gentle on digestion
items.content: Soft‑cooked rice and creamy texture are easy to digest, making it suitable for children and sensitive stomachs.

items.title: Dairy allergy or lactose intolerance
items.content: Traditional recipes use milk; people with dairy sensitivities should use plant‑based alternatives.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Rice can raise blood sugar quickly, so portion control is important for diabetics.

items.title: Added sugar content
items.content: Excess sugar increases calories and may contribute to tooth decay.

items.title: Risk of spoilage
items.content: Improper storage can lead to bacterial growth; keep the pudding refrigerated and consume within 2‑3 days.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve rice pudding warm or chilled, topped with cinnamon, cocoa powder, nuts, or fresh berries. It works as a breakfast, dessert, or light snack.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the finished pudding in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat gently on the stove or in the microwave, adding a splash of milk or water to restore its creamy consistency.
